conclusion.summary: The meeting agreed to keep today's two dark cards exactly as they are and make them the first of three pages you can slide sideways. Three dots sit right under the cards, where you drew them, and they are buttons too, so nobody has to swipe. Page 2 is "Calories and protein this week": a bar for each day under the same M T W T F S S as the circles above, your target as a dashed line, and your average calories and protein a day over the days you logged. Page 3 is "Today: sugar, salt and fibre", using only figures that labels and menus print, with no targets and no colours. New people learn it from a one-line hint under the dots, one slow slide of the cards and one added sentence in Pip's "Your day" tip. The hint goes once they have seen page 2, or after 5 days. It will be built on the iap branch only, and nothing goes live until you say.

pages.title: Calories and protein this week
pages.shows:
One wide dark card (DARK_CARD: #1d2320, white words, lime #d6efa0), as wide as page 1's two cards together and exactly page 1's height. The card is a flex column. Its chart area is flex-1 with a minimum of about 64pt, so the bars shrink or grow to fill whatever room the title, averages and notes leave.

Title: "Calories and protein this week" at the top left, in 0.875rem bold white, sentence case (readable, not only 11px capitals). It may wrap to two lines in Italian or Portuguese.

Averages: two figures side by side, mirroring page 1's left and right.
- The calories average in lime ("1,840", 1.25rem, app-numbers), with "kcal a day" under it.
- The protein average in lime ("96g"), with "protein a day" under it.
- Under both, in 0.8125rem white/70: "From the 3 days you logged, not counting today."

Legend: just above the chart, at the right, a short dashed swatch and "Your target: 2,000 kcal" (0.75rem DM Mono, white/75). It sits off the title row so the longer title and the legend never fight for one line.

Chart: seven columns, Monday to Sunday of weekOf(now). They sit on the exact grid of the day circles above (grid-cols-7 gap-2 across the full card width, no side padding of their own), so Tuesday's bar sits straight under Tuesday's circle.
- Each logged column has the day's calories in 11px DM Mono white/75, then a lime bar: rounded top, about 55% of the column width, starting from zero, height = calories / top of scale.
- The top of the scale is max(target, highest day) x 1.15. A logged day's bar is at least 3px tall.
- Under each bar is the narrow weekday letter (11px white/60). Today's letter sits in a small lime pill, like today's circle.
- A dashed 1px white/40 line crosses the chart at settings.dailyCalories. A bar past the line stays the same lime: no red, no "over".
- A past day with no entries has no bar and no figure, only a short white/25 dash on the baseline. It is never drawn or counted as 0.
- Days still to come show only a dim letter (white/30).
- Today's bar is drawn like the others (so far).
- The bars are drawn still: they don't grow when the page appears.
- The chart cannot be tapped. The circles directly above already open each day.

Card foot, in 0.8125rem white/70, each line only when it applies:
- "Some meals this week have no protein entered, so protein counts only the rest."
- "Includes estimates from your photos."

How it is worked out (pure lib/mm/week.ts, unit-tested first; date helpers stay in lib/mm/day.ts):
- weekOf(now) moves from page.tsx into lib/mm/day.ts, beside startOfDay, dayParam, loggedDayKeys and the Monday-first monthGrid. page.tsx's own dayKey format is dropped in favour of dayParam, which loggedDayKeys already uses.
- Days are built with new Date(y, m, d+i), never by stepping back 24h from now.
- A day's calories = the sum of nutrients.calories of the entries whose dayParam(new Date(loggedAt)) is that day. Portions are already scaled.
- Counted days = days this week before today with at least one entry.
- Calories average = the sum over the counted days / the number of counted days, shown with formatInt.
- Protein average = the sum of nutrients.protein over the counted days' entries that have it / the number of counted days with at least one protein figure, shown with formatGrams.
- When there is no protein figure, the protein average shows a "–" that is hidden from screen readers, with spoken text "none yet".
- Never divided by 7. A day with nothing logged is never counted as 0. Today is never in an average.
- The gap note shows when any entry in the counted days has no protein.
- The estimate note shows when any entry this week up to now has estimate: true.
- Entries dated after today are ignored.
- The log is filtered to the week first, and the result is memoised on [log, dayParam(now)], because the log is kept for ever and Home re-renders every minute.

pages.title: Today: sugar, salt and fibre
pages.shows:
One wide dark card, the same size as page 2 (page 1's height), with the title "Today: sugar, salt and fibre" (0.875rem bold white).

Three rows, in the title's order: Sugar, Salt, Fibre. They are spread evenly over the card's height and split by a thin white/10 line. Each is drawn like page 1's MacroRow, but with no target and no bar:
- The name sits at the left in 11px bold spaced capitals, white/75.
- Today's figure sits at the right in 0.9375rem DM Mono white. It is bigger than page 1's because there is no bar and the figure is the point.
- Under the figure, only when some of today's foods didn't give it, in 0.8125rem white/60: "from 3 of your 4 foods".

How it is worked out (pure lib/mm/labelTotals.ts todayLabelTotals(log, now), unit-tested first):
- n = all of today's entries. Typed entries and photo estimates count in n but never carry these figures.
- For each nutrient, k = today's entries where that field (nutrients.sugar / salt / fiber) is a finite number of 0 or more. sanitizeLog only checks calories, protein, carbs and fat, so a bad stored value (NaN, a negative number, a string) is skipped here and tested.
- The sum is taken over those k entries. sumNutrients already keeps a partial figure off a combined entry, so each entry's figure is either complete or absent.
- When k = 0, the row shows "not published" in place of a figure.
- The figures use the same formatters as the item page's NutrientTable, so Home and the item pages always agree: formatOptionalGrams for sugar and fibre, and formatSalt for salt (up to 2 decimals, as UK guides print it).
- Sodium is never turned into salt, and salt is never turned into sodium.

There are no targets, reference intakes, bars, colours, traffic lights or high/low words.

Footer, in 0.8125rem white/70: "Only foods whose label or menu gives these figures are counted."

This page looks clearly different from pages 1 and 2 (rows, not a dial or bars). It uses figures the app already keeps on every logged food but never adds up anywhere. A recipe logged from the meal plan now carries its sugar, salt and fibre too (see the build list), so it is not wrongly counted as "not given".
pages.empty_state:
Nothing logged today (Premium): each row shows a "–" that is hidden from screen readers, with spoken text "nothing logged yet". Then come the line "Nothing logged yet today." and the footer.

If today's foods are all from calories-only chains or typed in, all three rows read "not published".

conclusion.dots:
Placement: centred directly under the cards, where the founder drew them, in the app's own colours (the purple was just the pen).
- The row is `relative z-10 flex justify-center` and starts at the cards' bottom edge. The strip's shadow padding is cancelled by its own negative margin, so the row sits over that padding, and the visible dots are centred about 22pt below the cards.
- Under the dots come, as today: the first-visit hint (while it shows), today's gap line, the free card, StartPrompt and the set-targets card. Then Scan your food.
- Home's wrapper around RecipeTools (mt-1 today) is tightened.

The "at most about 24pt" drop of the Scan card holds only in the settled state: the hint is gone, the user is Premium and there is no gap sentence. While the hint shows it adds about 44pt more. For a free user, the upsell card sits in between as it does today. Both states are screenshotted at 393pt and the measured drops are written in docs/PROGRESS_LOG.md, so nobody later "fixes" the first-visit layout to meet a target it was never meant to meet.

Buttons: three real <button type="button">, each 44x44pt and touching, so the dots are 44pt apart (the drawing shows about 42pt) and every tap target meets the 44pt rule. They sit in <div role="group" aria-label="Choose what to show">.

Look:
- Pages not shown: 10px circles in --muted #5f6361. That is about 5.6:1 on the #f4f5f6 page, above the 3:1 needed for controls, and the same grey as the M T W T F S S letters above. The 25-35% opacity versions in some proposals (about 1.5:1) were rejected as invisible to older eyes.
- Page shown: a 24x10 pill in the cards' own dark #1d2320, so "you are here" shows by shape as well as colour.
- No lime (too faint on light grey) and no purple.
- The width and colour change over 200ms, and instantly with reduced motion.
- Focus: the app's accent outline, offset 2px, rounded-full.

Names: aria-label "Today", "Calories and protein this week" and "Sugar, salt and fibre". These are plain words, so Voice Control's "Tap Calories and protein this week" works. The page shown has aria-current="true".

Tapping a dot calls scroller.scrollTo({ left: index x step x (rtl ? -1 : 1), behavior: reduced motion ? "auto" : "smooth" }). Step is the measured distance between page 1's and page 2's starts. It is not scrollIntoView, so Home never also jerks up or down. Focus stays on the dot.

The current dot follows the scroll position (see swipe), so the dots and the cards always agree. In column mode, when the cards stack, the dots are display:none.
conclusion.swipe:
Only the browser's own scrolling is used: no new dependency, no touch code, no swipe library.

Structure (new web/app/app/_components/HomePages.tsx):
- A wrapper at content width holds the strip, the dots row and the hint. It carries data-coach="home-numbers", so Pip's spotlight covers the cards and dots at 353pt, not the full screen. It is a CSS container (Tailwind v4 @container) and has a ResizeObserver that tells the script about column mode (width < 20.375 x the root font size, the same threshold as the container query and PAIR).
- The strip is the scroller. It runs edge to edge like the Recipes carousel (-mx-5), so a sliding card leaves at the edge of the glass, not at an invisible clip line 20pt in.
- Scroller settings:
  - overflow-x: auto and overflow-y: hidden. WebKit backs overflow with a UIScrollView, and even 1px of vertical overflow would let it catch vertical drags.
  - scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; overscroll-behavior-x: contain; .no-scrollbar; scroll-padding-inline: 20px.
  - padding-bottom 2rem with margin-bottom -2rem, so the cards' 40px drop shadow isn't clipped.
  - tabIndex 0, for keyboard arrows and axe's scrollable-region-focusable rule, with a focus-visible ring only, so a finger tap never outlines the cards.
- Inside the scroller, a flex track holds the 20px start and end padding (on the track, not the scroller, because WebKit can drop a scroller's end padding) with a 40px gap.
- Each page is width: 100cqw (the wrapper's content width; not 100%, because the scroller is 40px wider than the content), shrink-0, scroll-snap-align: start and scroll-snap-stop: always.
- Page 1 sets the height. Pages 2 and 3 are flex columns that fill it: page 2's chart is flex-1 with a minimum of about 64pt, and page 3's three rows spread over the height. The strip may grow past page 1's height only if the longest real language (Italian or Portuguese) or both of page 2's notes at once still overflow at 375pt.
- At rest, page 1 sits exactly where the cards are now and nothing peeks, because the 40px gap equals the two 20px gutters.

Gestures:
- No touchstart or touchmove listeners, no preventDefault, and touch-action stays auto. WebKit locks each drag to one direction itself:
  - a mostly vertical drag that starts on the cards scrolls Home;
  - a sideways drag moves exactly one page (snap-stop means a hard fling can't skip page 2);
  - a diagonal drag is decided by WebKit.
- No wrap-around from page 3 to page 1, and no auto-advance.
- The current page = Math.round(|scrollLeft| / step), read in a passive scroll listener throttled to one animation frame. The |...| makes Arabic and Urdu work, where scrollLeft is negative and the order flips by itself.
- The iOS back-swipe (WebAppView.swift:29, allowsBackForwardNavigationGestures = true) still owns a drag that starts at the very left edge, as it does on Home today. Either result of an edge drag on page 2 is acceptable, and the first dot is the sure way back to Today.
- No change to the Swift app.

Feel: like the iPhone's own paged cards. One page per swipe, the pill moves as the page settles, the dial's fill animation stays on page 1, and the week bars are drawn still.

What is remembered:
- Nothing about the page. Home always opens on Today, and the pages contain no links, so there is nothing to come Back to.
- One small per-device store, homePagesStore in lib/mm/stores.ts ("mm.v1.homePages", made with createStore like tourStore, with a sanitizer). It holds { seen, slid, hintDays, lastHintDay }.
  - It is not synced and not in SYNCED_SETTING_KEYS: seen and dismissed flags stay on one device, as dismissedTargetsCard does.
  - It is reset by "Clear data on this device" and by "Reset onboarding" in settings/page.tsx.
  - If storage fails, the store falls back to memory: the slide may not play, and the hint may show again.
- seen is set the first time page 2 or 3 is shown by any means (swipe, dot or hint).

How a first-time user learns it:
1. The dots themselves.
2. The hint line under the dots, which is itself a 44pt button: "Slide the cards sideways, or tap here, to see your week" (0.875rem semibold, accent colour, centred), followed by the existing ChevronRightIcon. The icon is aria-hidden and already flips in right-to-left languages.
   - Tapping it goes to page 2.
   - It shows only while seen is false, and on at most 5 separate days: hintDays counts the days it was shown, using dayParam. After either, it is gone for good, so people who don't care about stats get a clean Home back.
   - The words never say left or right, because people disagree about which way a swipe goes (the founder's own "swipe right" shows it).
3. One demonstration slide. It plays once per device: the first time Home shows with the hint visible, no Pip tip due on Home (coachDue(coachStore, "home") is false when Home opens), reduced motion off and not in column mode.
   - If Pip's tips are due on that visit, the slide waits for a later Home visit. It never fires straight after the overlay closes.
   - About 1s after Home shows, the track moves about 80pt towards page 2, so about 40pt of page 2's dark edge slides in, then back, over 700ms.
   - It uses a CSS transform on the track, not scrollBy, because mandatory snap would cancel a partial scroll. It is mirrored in right-to-left languages, and slid is set when it starts.
4. Pip's existing "Your day" tip (coachSteps.ts) lights the cards and the dots together, and its text becomes: "What you've eaten today and what's left. Slide the cards or tap the dots to see your week." That is 90 characters with no digits, within coach.test.ts's 130-character limit. Settings › Help › "Show me the buttons on each screen" replays it. There is no new eighth tip on Home.

In column mode, when the cards stack: no strip, no dots, no hint, no slide.
accessibility: The strip is <div role="region" aria-label="Your numbers" tabIndex={0}> with a focus-visible ring, so a tap never draws one. Keyboard arrow keys scroll it natively, page by page. There is no aria-roledescription "carousel" or "slide": those words mean nothing to most older VoiceOver users.

Each page is role="group" with aria-label "{name}, {n} of 3": "Today, 1 of 3", "Calories and protein this week, 2 of 3", "Today: sugar, salt and fibre, 3 of 3". Pages off screen are never aria-hidden, inert or display:none, so VoiceOver reads page 1, then 2, then 3 in order.

No focusin handler: the pages hold nothing focusable, so it would almost never run. The real test is on the device: with VoiceOver in the packed app (WKWebView), moving the cursor into page 2 must bring it into view. If it doesn't, that is fixed before release, and the dots are always there as the plain way to switch.

Headings: page 1 gets a screen-reader-only h2 "Today". Pages 2 and 3 use their visible titles as h2, so the rotor's Headings jump between pages. No page is named "This week", because the circles' <ol aria-label="This week"> already has that name and e2e locators would clash.

Dots: a group "Choose what to show" of three <button>s, each 44x44pt, named "Today", "Calories and protein this week" and "Sugar, salt and fibre", with aria-current="true" on the page shown and a visible focus outline. Focus stays on the dot after a tap.

The hint line is a real button, at least 44pt tall. Its chevron is the existing ChevronRightIcon: aria-hidden and flipped for right-to-left, so VoiceOver never reads a "›" and it never points the wrong way in Arabic or Urdu.

Placeholders: every "–" (page 2's protein average with no figure; page 3's rows with nothing logged) is aria-hidden, with screen-reader text "none yet" or "nothing logged yet", so VoiceOver never says "en dash".

Week chart: the drawn bars, figures, letters and dashed line are aria-hidden. A screen-reader-only <ol aria-label="Calories each day"> gives each day from Monday to today: "{day}: {n} kcal", "{day} (today, so far): {n} kcal" or "{day}: nothing logged" (day from the existing longDay formatter, e.g. "Tuesday 17 November"). The chart has no links, so there are no extra tab stops or duplicate link names.
Sugar, salt and fibre: each row is plain text in reading order (name, figure, then "from k of your n foods" when shown), so VoiceOver hears the partial-sum note with its figure.

Page 1's existing bars and dial get aria-valuetext with the real figures ("56 grams of 150 grams"; "640 of 2,000 kcal, 1,360 left"). Today VoiceOver hears only a percentage capped at 100. The dial keeps its name "Calories used today".

Contrast: inactive dots #5f6361 on #f4f5f6 are about 5.6:1. White/70 text on #1d2320 is well above 4.5:1. The dashed target line is decorative and is explained by its text legend "Your target: {n} kcal". Nothing relies on colour alone: the current dot is a pill, and the target is labelled in words.
Reduced motion: no demonstration slide; dot taps jump straight to the page; no pill transition; the bars never animate.

Large text and narrow screens: when PAIR stacks (content under 20.375rem, from a container query for the styles and a ResizeObserver for the script), all three pages show one under another with their titles, and the dots, hint and slide are hidden. Note: the iPhone app doesn't follow iOS Larger Text (TEXT_SIZE_CHOICE_ENABLED is false), so this happens on 320pt screens and at website zoom.
Right-to-left (Arabic, Urdu): page and dot order flip by themselves, |scrollLeft| keeps the current page right, scrollTo uses a negative left, the slide is mirrored and the hint's chevron flips.

axe stays at 0 on "home" and "home (free)" in e2e/a11y.mjs (scrollable-region-focusable, label-content-name-mismatch, aria-allowed-attr). a11y.mjs sets the per-device "slid" flag first, so axe never runs mid-slide. The hint stays visible there, so axe covers it.
other_improvements: The calories dial shows the real percentage (115% when 2,300 of 2,000 kcal), with the ring full and in the same lime, no warning colour. Today it is capped at 100% (page.tsx: used = Math.min(1, ...)), which is an untrue figure. This is built only after the founder's yes (founder question 2). '{n} over' stays white like '{n} left', and a test checks it never turns red.
Spoken values (aria-valuetext) with the real figures on the dial and on the protein, carbs and fat bars. Gauge gets a valueText prop, and MacroRow builds "{eaten} grams of {target} grams".

Today's gap sentence stays where it is, under the dots (and under the hint while it shows). It doesn't change with the page, so nothing below jumps while swiping. It gains "today" so it is true under any page: "Some meals you added today have no protein, carbs or fat entered, so today's figures only count the rest." Notes about the week sit inside page 2's card. The Today page keeps the old sentence.
The free card "Log your meals to see what's left today." stays the single upsell, unchanged, under the dots and hint. Pages 2 and 3 never add a second button.

Pip's "Your day" tip: the data-coach="home-numbers" spotlight moves to the wrapper around the cards and dots (content width). Its text becomes "What you've eaten today and what's left. Slide the cards or tap the dots to see your week." (90 characters, no digits).

weekOf() moves from page.tsx into lib/mm/day.ts, beside startOfDay, dayParam, loggedDayKeys and monthGrid. page.tsx's private dayKey format is replaced by dayParam / loggedDayKeys, so the day circles and the week chart share one definition of a day and of "this week".

Scan your food entries get an optional estimate: true on LogEntry. It is written by scan/page.tsx log() and kept by sanitizeLog only when it is exactly true. This makes "Includes estimates from your photos." reliable without matching the translated "(estimate)" name. Older entries can't be flagged, and the note says only what is flagged (Scan your food isn't released anywhere yet, so there are almost none).

A recipe logged from the meal plan (plan/page.tsx logMine, about line 834) today keeps only kcal, protein, carbs and fat. It is changed to log through recipeNutrients, the same as Add food's RecipePick, so its sugar, salt, fibre, saturated fat and kJ come with it wherever every product printed them. Otherwise page 3 would wrongly count plan recipes as "not given".
The first-visit flags live in one small per-device store (homePagesStore, "mm.v1.homePages"). It is not synced, and it is cleared by "Clear data on this device" and "Reset onboarding".
The two dark cards move into their own component (HomeToday.tsx, moved as they are, no visual change), and the pages live in HomePages.tsx, HomeWeek.tsx and HomeLabels.tsx, so page.tsx stays small.

Spacing: the dots row replaces most of today's gap between the cards and Scan your food. In the settled state (hint gone, Premium, no gap sentence), the Scan card drops by no more than about 24pt. The first-visit and free-user states are measured and recorded separately.
not_doing: A sliver of the next card always showing at the right edge. It is the strongest hint, but it changes the founder's measured layout, puts a card under iOS's forward-swipe edge, and needs mirroring for Arabic. It goes to the founder as a question (recommended: not now). The one-time slide shows the same edge once instead.

Auto-sliding on every visit, a bounce on each of the first 3 visits, or any movement without words on screen. Unexplained movement reads as "did I touch something?" and turns into nagging. The slide plays once per device, only with the hint showing and never straight after Pip's overlay.

Keeping the hint line for ever for people who never swipe. It would push Scan your food down by 44pt on every visit. It retires after 5 days even if page 2 was never seen; the dots and Pip's tip still teach it after that.

Syncing the "seen" flag between devices: seen and dismissed flags stay on one device, as dismissedTargetsCard does, and syncing it would mean adding to SYNCED_SETTING_KEYS and docs/ACCOUNTS_SYNC.md for no real gain.

Page 2 titled only "Calories this week" while it also shows protein: a title must name everything on its page. Dropping the protein average was rejected too, because protein is half of what the app is for.
"Your target now" in the legend: "now" reads oddly to an ordinary reader. "Your target: {n} kcal" is plain and still true.
A legend on the same row as the title: the longer title and the legend can't share one line at 353pt, so the legend sits just above the chart.
"Past 7 days" in the same dial-and-bars layout as Today: someone who swipes by accident would take the averages for today's figures. Every page must look clearly different.

A rolling "last 7 days" window: its letters wouldn't line up with the Mon-Sun circles directly above, which puts two different weeks on one screen. Monday's near-empty week is covered by "A new week starts today." and last week's average.

"Protein this week" as a second, near-identical bar chart page (and the outlined bars for partial protein that went with it): a swipe would show the same picture twice. Protein is instead the second headline figure on page 2.
Last 30 days: abstract and slow to read. Only about 2 days of the log sync between devices, so on a second phone it would be built from almost nothing.
Protein at each meal as a page: it repeats the meal rows just below.
Today's meal plan as page 3: most people would see an empty advert inside "Your numbers". It would also need the recipe book in Home's bundle and new synced fields, and the plan is only on one phone.

Top foods, Most protein and Added most: grouping by name is fragile across languages and portions, an AI estimate could top a ranked list next to a food's name (rule 1), and "Brownie, 5 times" reads as a judgement (rule 3).

Streaks, "days on target", "5 of 7", ticks, badges, red, "over" or "under" on the week page, and a standing this-week-against-last-week comparison: they score the person (rule 3), as reminders.ts already refuses. Last week's average appears only on Monday, with no arrows.
Targets, reference intakes, traffic lights or high/low words on sugar, salt and fibre: these are a health judgement (rule 3) and a new limit (rule 8).
A saturated fat row on page 3: the title must name everything on the page, and a fourth row crowds the card. Three packet words are recognised fastest.
A sodium row, or turning sodium into salt: that would be a figure the source did not print.
Rounding salt to one decimal on Home: the item pages show up to 2 decimals (formatSalt), and Home must agree with them.
Week bars as links to each day: below 44pt on narrow screens, 7 more VoiceOver stops that repeat the circles' links, and a tap fighting the swipe. The circles directly above already open each day.
A focusin handler to scroll focused pages into view: the pages hold nothing focusable, so it would almost never run. The VoiceOver check on the device is the real test.
Remembering the last page shown, or restoring it on Back: Home must look the same every time it opens.
Pro/Premium buttons inside pages 2 and 3, and sample or decorative bars for free users: a second upsell within a hand's width, and invented-looking data (rule 1).
A new, separate Pip tip for the dots: Home keeps its seven tips, and the existing "Your day" tip covers the cards and dots together.
Moving the dots above the cards at large text: a control that changes place gets lost. The pages stack instead.
A Protein/Calories switch inside page 2: a hidden control inside a page that is itself behind a swipe.
JavaScript touch handlers, touch-action: pan-x, a swipe library, or switching off the iOS back gesture in Swift: these fight vertical scrolling, add a dependency (rule 6) or need a native build.

Playwright WebKit runs for the new e2e: no e2e script uses Playwright's WebKit today, and getting it means a browser download the founder would have to approve, on a Mac that is short of disk. The gesture checks are done in the Simulator and on the iPhone instead.
Widening the food log's sync window so the week matches on every device: that is a privacy change (rule 4, the privacy page, the App Privacy answers), so it is put to the founder as a question.
Water on these pages: water entries are kept only 14 days and are not synced, and the Water card already shows today.
Spotting photo estimates by their name ending in "(estimate)": the name is translated when logged, so the check fails in 10 of 11 languages. The new estimate flag is used instead.
Making page 1's cards a link to /app/today: older users often tap-drag, so swipes would turn into navigation. The meal rows already open the day.
Later, separately, not in this change: protein on each meal row, "Open today's plan" on the Meal plan card, sugar, salt and fibre on the day page, and following iOS Larger Text in the iPhone app.

founder_questions: Should a thin edge of the next card always show at the right of the screen, as a hint that the cards slide? Recommended: No, not now. It changes the card layout you had measured to the pixel and puts a card under the iPhone's forward-swipe edge. The tappable dots, the hint line (shown for up to 5 days), the one-time slide and Pip's tip do the job. If the older testers still don't find page 2, we add it then.

The calories dial says 100% when someone has eaten more than their target (2,300 of 2,000 kcal shows 100%). Should it show the real figure (115%), with the ring full and in the same lime, no warning colour? Recommended: Yes, because every figure on screen must be true (rule 1). It is built only after your yes.

Only the last 2 days of the food log sync between devices, so the new week page shows only the days logged on that phone (or on the website). Should the whole week sync? Recommended: Not now. It changes what we keep on the server, so the privacy page and the App Store privacy answers would need updating. The wording ("the days you logged", "on this device") stays true either way.
